findings.issue: Outline section 2 says '$34,000 and $36,250 totals'. 25,500 + 11,750 = 37,250 (2026 equivalent 35,750 is on the live 2026 guide). $36,250 is not in IRS IR-2026-136 or Notice 2026-66.
findings.fix: Change to $34,000 (age 50+) and $37,250 (ages 60-63, calculated from IRS $25,500 + $11,750), label the sum as our calculation; add both totals to the closed fact list and re-verify the 2026-vs-2027 table deltas ($1,000, $500, $500).

findings.issue: Roth catch-up wage threshold section is under-specified. Notice 2026-66 words it as the Roth catch-up wage threshold 'for 2026' used to decide whether 2027 catch-ups must be Roth ($150,000 to $155,000). The outline could be written as 'earn over $155,000 in 2027', and employer/FICA-wage detail is not in the saved sources.
findings.fix: Quote the notice wording in the fact list (threshold applied to wages measured a year earlier, only for catch-ups, plan-specific), forbid unsourced detail (FICA, same-employer) unless added from a saved primary source, and state the plan-adoption caveat.

findings.issue: Working answer says under 400% FPL 'a lower-priced plan or updated income can restore a credit'. A cheaper plan does not restore a credit (credit = benchmark silver minus income contribution, capped at the chosen plan premium, per the page's own formula); it lowers the net premium. HIGH-profile consequential claim, unsupported by KFF/HealthCare.gov.
findings.fix: Rewrite: below 400% FPL you still get a credit (smaller than under the expired enhanced credits); a corrected income estimate changes the credit; a cheaper or bronze plan lowers what you pay but trades premium for deductible; above 400% FPL there is no credit by law (KFF). Keep consistent with the existing formula and 'Updating income' sections.

findings.issue: (a) Action row states 'December 15 / January 15' without the platform caveat BUILD recorded in readiness (HealthCare.gov dates apply to the HealthCare.gov platform; state exchanges vary). (b) KFF +58% ($113 to $178) and +37% deductible are 2026 vs 2025 figures; row context risks presenting them as 2027. (c) Readiness says 'official sources only' but KFF is a research nonprofit.
findings.fix: Carry the state-exchange caveat into the answer, date every KFF figure (2026 vs 2025; 2027 benchmark silver +13%), name KFF visibly as the source, and correct the readiness wording. Do not use the X-post Wisconsin 22% or $1,800 figures (already excluded).
